subject: Chemistry
title: The Orange That Turns Green: Potassium Dichromate
summary: Potassium dichromate is made from chromite ore: fusion with sodium carbonate in air gives yellow sodium chromate (Fe₂O₃ is filtered off), acid turns it into orange sodium dichromate (two CrO₄ tetrahedra share one oxygen), and KCl precipitates the less soluble K₂Cr₂O₇. Chromate and dichromate interconvert with pH while Cr stays +6. In acid, Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O (E° = 1.33 V): a strong oxidising agent that turns orange to green, oxidising Fe²⁺, I⁻, H₂S and, in the 1954 breathalyser, ethanol.

notes.title: 14 – Potassium Dichromate: Preparation and Oxidising Action

keyPoints: **Chromite** (FeCr₂O₄) + Na₂CO₃ + air → **yellow Na₂CrO₄**; Fe₂O₃ is filtered off.
Acid: **2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O** (orange); base reverses it. Cr stays **+6**: not redox.
In acid **Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O**: orange → green, a strong oxidiser (Fe²⁺, I⁻, H₂S, ethanol).

blocks.p: 1 mol Cr₂O₇²⁻ accepts 6 mol e⁻, so it oxidises 6 mol Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺, or 6 mol I⁻ to 3 mol I₂.
